title: Poisoning Toxidromes: Cholinergic Versus Anticholinergic
subject: Forensic Medicine
preview: A cholinergic toxidrome includes bronchorrhea, bradycardia, lacrimation, sweating and gastrointestinal hyperactivity.
quickRevision: A cholinergic toxidrome includes bronchorrhea, bradycardia, lacrimation, sweating and gastrointestinal hyperactivity.
Airway support and decontamination or antidotes depend on the substance and circumstances.
Mixed intoxication may produce overlapping signs; toxicology advice may be needed.

sections.title: Recognize the core pattern
points: A cholinergic toxidrome includes bronchorrhea, bradycardia, lacrimation, sweating and gastrointestinal hyperactivity.
An anticholinergic toxidrome more often has dry flushed skin, mydriasis, tachycardia and urinary retention.

sections.title: Clinical examination and interpretation
points: Airway support and decontamination or antidotes depend on the substance and circumstances.
Mixed intoxication may produce overlapping signs; toxicology advice may be needed.

sections.title: Exam trap — avoid this mistake
points: Use the whole pattern rather than one pupil finding to decide between toxidromes.
